capabilities.target: container shell with full workspace and environment access
git branch on GitHub, reachable org-wide by the mounted PAT

inputs.source: GitHub issue title and body on a public repository
Repository file contents read during reproduction and testing

instructions.note: The agent is told to pick up any bug-labeled issue and run whatever commands it needs, with no boundary on command type, target, or scope.
The sole barrier against deleting data or exfiltrating secrets is a single prompt line, with no structural denylist, sandboxed egress, or credential scoping behind it.
The injection defense (ignore instructions inside issues or code) is itself a behavioral instruction with no spotlighting, delimiting, or classifier support.
The agent is given standing authority to edit its own .agent/config.yaml whenever it judges it needs extra tools, with no approval step and no limit on what it may add.

controls.name: Prompt rule against destructive or exfiltration commands
controls.decay_rationale: Purely behavioral; a hijacked or more capable model can rationalize exceptions or split the forbidden action into steps that each look permitted.

controls.name: Prompt rule to ignore instructions embedded in issues or code
controls.decay_rationale: Behavioral injection defense with no structural spotlighting or classifier behind it; a sufficiently persuasive embedded instruction defeats it, and that gets easier as the model gets better at following longer injected goals.

controls.name: Container execution on a shared CI runner
controls.decay_rationale: The isolation mechanism itself does not decay with model capability, but it does not close this design's two main escape vectors: network is declared unrestricted and the org-wide PAT is mounted directly into the container's environment, so it earns no credit against exfiltration or credential misuse.

controls.name: Runtime write protection on .agent/config.yaml
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by OS or orchestrator file permissions outside the model; makes the self-config sink unreachable regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Human approval gate before self-configuration changes
Human approval gate before pushing outside the originating repository
Bounded step count, runtime, and compute rate limit
Audit logging of shell, write, push, and config-change actions
Egress, credential-scoping, and identity-pinning controls for the planned Slack MCP server

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted issue content drives arbitrary shell execution with an org-wide credential and unrestricted egress

attack_path.note: Any GitHub user can open an issue and add the bug label via the issue template, making this an untrusted, attacker-reachable entry point.
The agent runs whatever commands it judges necessary, with the org-wide PAT in its environment and unrestricted outbound network, so it can read secrets or files and send them out in one action.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: model is declared as 'latest' with swappable:true, so upgrades already happen without review; also watch median steps or runtime per task trending upward.

evidence.observation: network: unrestricted and env.GITHUB_TOKEN is an org-wide PAT with repo+workflow scope on all org repos, both reachable from the same shell the agent can run arbitrary commands in.
Any GitHub user can open issues and add the bug label through an issue template, so the triggering content is untrusted by default.
The only stated control against exfiltration is one prompt instruction, which is behavioral and model-dependent.

recommendations.action: Add a network egress allowlist restricting shell.run's outbound destinations to known-necessary endpoints, blocking arbitrary attacker-controlled destinations.
Scope the GitHub PAT to least privilege (single repo, minimal permissions) rather than an org-wide repo+workflow token mounted into the shell.
Log all shell commands and outbound network calls, reviewed on a cadence.

findings.title: Self-modification (TC3): the agent is authorized to edit its own .agent/config.yaml with no approval gate

attack_path.note: Untrusted issue content can include text intended to convince the agent it needs extra tools to finish the task.
The prompt explicitly authorizes editing .agent/config.yaml for extra tools, with no approval gate, and fs.write already has access to the whole workspace including .agent/.

forecast.watch_signal: model version change, or any further widening of autonomy or tool grants in .agent/config.yaml.

evidence.observation: The agent is told it may adjust .agent/config.yaml if it needs extra tools to finish a task, with no approval step.
autonomy: full and max_steps: null mean there is no runtime limit on how that self-configuration authority is used.

recommendations.action: Make .agent/config.yaml read-only to the agent's runtime identity; require a separate, human-approved deployment step to change agent configuration or tool grants.
Add a raw-action human approval gate before any self-configuration change takes effect.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): an org-wide PAT lets a single-repo bug-fix agent act across every repository in the org

attack_path.note: The org-wide repo+workflow-scoped PAT available in the shell is valid against every repository in the org, not only the one the issue was filed against.
github.push_branch, or an equivalent git command run directly in the shell, can push to any repository the PAT can reach.

forecast.watch_signal: widening of PAT scope, new repos added to the org, or model upgrade increasing susceptibility to being steered into other repos.

evidence.observation: GITHUB_TOKEN is commented as an org-wide PAT with repo + workflow scope on all org repos, far broader than the single repository the agent is meant to work on.

recommendations.action: Replace the org-wide PAT with a repository-scoped, minimally permissioned token so the agent cannot act outside the repository it was invoked for.
Add a human approval gate before any push to a repository other than the one the triggering issue came from.

findings.title: Unbounded steps and runtime on a shared CI runner create a denial-of-service and resource-exhaustion path (ASI08)

attack_path.note: A crafted issue, such as a reproduction step that never terminates, can be labeled bug by any outside user.
No max_unattended_steps or runtime limit is set (both null), and the agent runs on a shared CI runner, so an unbounded loop consumes shared resources indefinitely.

findings.residual_rationale: The only declared control that covers cap.shell (the prompt rule against deleting data or exfiltrating secrets) does not address unbounded step or runtime resource consumption; it provides no real mitigation for this denial-of-service path, so residual is rated at the inherent level rather than the mechanical credit floor.

forecast.watch_signal: median task runtime or step count per invocation trending upward on the shared CI runner.

evidence.observation: max_steps: null and autonomy: full, with no equivalent runtime cap declared.
Runs in a container on a shared CI runner, so unbounded execution affects shared infrastructure, not just the agent's own task.

recommendations.action: Set finite max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes, and add a compute or spend rate limit enforced by the orchestrator, not the model.
Add resource usage monitoring with automatic termination on the shared CI runner.

findings.title: Planned Slack MCP server would add a new egress channel to the same unmitigated, untrusted-issue-driven loop (ASI04)

attack_path.note: A planned Slack MCP server would give the agent a new send-capable channel reachable from the same untrusted-issue-driven reasoning loop, with no egress or credential controls described for it yet.

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

forecast.watch_signal: a new Slack MCP server entry appears in MCP client config or the tool manifest.

evidence.observation: The team wants to add a Slack MCP server next quarter, with no controls specified for it yet.

recommendations.action: Before connecting the Slack MCP server, apply the same egress allowlisting and credential scoping used elsewhere, require pinned tool definitions, and verify server identity.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted, publicly-openable GitHub issue reaches a fully autonomous (A4) agent holding an org-wide repo+workflow PAT, unrestricted network egress, and standing authority to rewrite its own configuration, with no approval gate anywhere in the design. Residual risk is already critical at the rollup level: three findings (exfiltration, self-modification, confused deputy across org repos) are pulled down to high by two behavioral prompt instructions, but the fourth finding (unbounded steps and runtime on a shared CI runner) has no applicable declared control at all and stays at the inherent level. Forecast risk stays critical because a model upgrade or any increase in autonomy removes the only credited controls (the two dependent prompt instructions), and because the model is already declared as 'latest' with no version pin, that decay condition is effectively already live rather than a future contingency. The planned Slack MCP server would add a further egress channel under the same unmitigated conditions.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, .agent/config.yaml, and the accompanying runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest or MCP configuration with argument-level schemas was provided; the exact blast radius of shell.run and fs.write is inferred from config.yaml and the system prompt, so confidence on precise scope is medium in places.

No approval-gate, logging, or egress-control configuration was provided beyond what the artifacts state; the absence of such controls is inferred from silence in the artifacts, which could understate controls enforced elsewhere in the organization's deployment pipeline.

The Slack MCP server addition is based on a stated intention ('next quarter') with no configuration yet; the related finding is forecast-only and should be reassessed once that integration is designed.
